verdicts.summary: On git older than 2.31, the combined rev-parse exit code is wrong, so the fallback reports an existing HEAD as absent. The note's claim that old git only echoes --path-format is not what happens.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Git 2.30 or older runs `rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir --git-path index --verify --quiet HEAD` in a repo with a committed HEAD. Git does not recognise --path-format, and with --verify an unrecognised non-revision argument makes rev-parse exit 1 with no stdout (quiet die). This is from my knowledge of git's rev-parse.c, not from this checkout. 2) VcsProcess.ts:304 does not throw because allowNonZeroExit is set; it returns exitCode 1 and empty stdout (VcsProcess.ts:336-344). 3) Line 852 sets headExists=false and line 853 sets headChecked=true. 4) lines=[""], length 1 != 3, so the fallback runs at line 865. Line 868 is `headChecked ? headExists : hasHeadCommit`, which keeps headExists=false without calling hasHeadCommit. 5) At 939 the `if (headExists)` block is skipped, so the temp index is not seeded with `read-tree HEAD`. At 1212 commit-tree gets no `-p HEAD`. The checkpoint is a parentless commit, and gitignored files tracked in HEAD are missing from its tree because `add -A` skips ignored paths the index does not contain. The old code (hasHeadCommit at its own call) returned true here. Consequence: a silently different checkpoint on older Git (Ubuntu 20.04 ships 2.25, for example), with no error. If git echoes the flag instead, exit is 0 and this path is not reached, so the outcome depends on that git behaviour, which I could not open here.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:939-959 (headExists gates read-tree HEAD and the reused index)
apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:221 and 304-344 (allowNonZeroExit returns exit 1 with stdout)
apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:279-287 and 361-366 (no retry or fsync path for allowNonZeroExit)
verdicts.consequence: On git < 2.31 the checkpoint loses its HEAD parent and HEAD's gitignored tracked files, with no error. Restore and diff behaviour then depends on the checkpoint contents.
verdicts.missing: Git source for rev-parse.c (unknown --path-format under --verify) is not in the checkout. The verdict assumes it exits 1; a test on git 2.30 would settle it. Restore consequences were not read.

verdicts.summary: For an unborn HEAD, the combined call now exits 1 under the CHECKPOINT_CAPTURE_OPERATION label, so the failure is counted against capture rather than hasHeadCommit.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Capture runs in a repo with no commits. 2) The combined call uses operation CHECKPOINT_CAPTURE_OPERATION with allowNonZeroExit, so it exits 1. 3) VcsProcess.ts:221 sets failedExit=true, and VcsProcess.ts:261-263 records outcome=failure under the capture operation. Before, the same failure was recorded under GitVcsDriver.checkpoints.hasHeadCommit. Consequence: the metric for the capture operation now shows failures for every unborn-HEAD capture. This is an attribution shift only, no behaviour change.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:76-84 (capture operation is a known metric label)
verdicts.consequence: Capture failure-rate dashboards count expected unborn-HEAD exits as failures.
